steps: لما العناصر تتداخل على الشاشة، نحتاج طريقة عشان نعرف مين يظهر فوق التاني وكأننا بنرتب ورق فوق بعضه في طابور. بنسمي الترتيب ده نظام الطبقات أو Stacking Context على صفحة الويب.
عشان نتحكم في مين فوق ومين تحت، بنستخدم خاصية CSS اسمها z-index. الخاصية دي بتدي أرقام صحيحة للعناصر المرتبة عشان تحدد مين يغطي التاني.
تخيل z-index زي طبقات الكيك أو أدوار العمارة؛ الدور اللي رقمه أكبر بيظهر قدامنا ومغطي الأدوار اللي تحته واللي أرقامها أصغر.
لو عندنا صندوقين فوق بعض وعايزين الصندوق الأصفر يظهر فوق الصندوق الأخضر، بندي الأصفر z-index أكبر زي 3 والأخضر z-index أصغر زي 2.
قاعدة ذهبية: خاصية z-index بتشتغل بس مع العناصر اللي ليها position زي absolute أو relative أو fixed، ومش بتشتغل مع position: static العادي.
بنستفيد من z-index في الحياة العملية لما بنعمل قوائم منسدلة Dropdown menus أو أزرار منبغشة Pop-ups تظهر فوق باقي محتوى الصفحة وماتختفيش وراه.
ar.example: لو عملنا مربعين متداخلين على الشاشة، المربع الأول الأخضر بياخد position: absolute و z-index: 2، والمربع التاني الذهبي بياخد position: absolute و z-index: 3. بما إن رقم 3 أكبر من رقم 2، هيظهر المربع الذهبي فوق المربع الأخضر ويغطيه كأنه كارت فوق كارت تاني.
ar.mistake: لو كتبت z-index: 10 لعنصر ومظهرش فوق العنصر التاني، غالباً نسيت تكتب خاصية position زي relative أو absolute للعنصر. الحل: تأكد إن العنصر عنده position مش static عشان z-index تشتغل معاك صح.
ar.recap: خاصية z-index بتساعدنا نرتب العناصر المتداخلة فوق بعضها باستخدام أرقام صحيحة. لازم العنصر يكون عنده position عشان الخاصية دي تشتغل وتتحكم في طبقات الصفحة.

q.t: إيه هي الخاصية اللي بنستخدمها عشان نتحكم في ترتيب طبقات العناصر المتداخلة؟
q.why: خاصية z-index هي المسؤولة عن تحديد مين يظهر فوق التاني في العناصر المتداخلة.

q.t: علشان z-index تشتغل مع العنصر، لازم يكون عنده أي نوع من الـ position؟
q.why: خاصية z-index لا تطبق على العناصر اللي فيها position: static.

q.t: عنصر عنده z-index: 5 وعنصر تاني عنده z-index: 2، مين اللي هيظهر فوق التاني؟
q.why: العنصر اللي عنده z-index أكبر يظهر فوق العنصر اللي عنده رقم أصغر.

steps: When elements overlap on a webpage, we need a way to decide which one appears on top, just like stacking papers in a pile. We call this ordering system Stacking Context.
To control which element is on top or bottom, we use the CSS property called z-index. This property assigns integer numbers to positioned elements to determine overlap.
Imagine z-index like cake layers or building floors; the floor with the larger number appears in front of us, covering the floors below with smaller numbers.
If we have two overlapping boxes and want the yellow box to sit on top of the green one, we give the yellow box a larger z-index like 3 and the green box a smaller z-index like 2.
Golden rule: The z-index property only works on elements with a position value like absolute, relative, or fixed. It does not work on normal position: static elements.
We use z-index in real life when building drop-down menus or pop-up modals so they appear cleanly above all other page content without getting hidden underneath.
en.example: If we create two overlapping boxes on the screen, the first green box gets position: absolute and z-index: 2, while the second gold box gets position: absolute and z-index: 3. Since 3 is greater than 2, the gold box appears on top of the green box and covers it like a card over another.
en.mistake: If you wrote z-index: 10 for an element and it did not appear on top of another, you likely forgot to set a position property like relative or absolute. Solution: Ensure the element has a position other than static for z-index to take effect.
en.recap: The z-index property helps us order overlapping elements using integer numbers. The element must have a position set for this property to control page layers.

q.t: Which property do we use to control the stacking order of overlapping elements?
q.why: The z-index property is responsible for determining stacking order among overlapping elements.

q.t: For z-index to work on an element, what type of position must it have?
q.why: The z-index property does not apply to elements with position: static.

q.t: An element has z-index: 5 and another has z-index: 2. Which one appears on top?
o: Element 5 because its number is larger
q.why: The element with the higher z-index value appears on top of the one with the smaller value.

sections.h: The Concept of Overlapping and Layers
sections.text: When we design web pages, elements sometimes move and fall on top of each other. In this case, the browser needs an organized system to know which one is drawn first and which appears on top, just like organizing paper on a desk where the top paper covers the bottom one.
sections.code:
Bottom
Top
sections.output: A pink box appears covering part of a blue box underneath it.

sections.text: We use the CSS z-index property to control the stacking order of elements. The name comes from the Z-axis in 3D dimensions, meaning coming towards you or moving away. A larger number means closer proximity and appearing above other elements.
sections.code:
Layer 1
Layer 2
sections.output: A yellow box labeled Layer 2 appears completely covering the orange box.

sections.text: The z-index property does not work on just any element; the element must have a position property set to a value like relative, absolute, or fixed. If an element's position is static, z-index will have no effect on it at all.
sections.output: A green box in its normal place without any effect from z-index.

sections.text: We don't just use positive numbers like 1, 5, and 10; we can also use negative numbers like -1 to push an element behind the page background or beneath other elements, as if it is hiding under the table.
sections.code:
Behind all
Normal
sections.output: A red box hiding underneath the cyan box due to the negative number.

sections.text: A stacking context is like an independent small world for part of a page. When an element gets an integer z-index (other than auto), it establishes a new stacking context for itself and its children, meaning their order is contained within and not compared to outside elements.
sections.output: An inner element following its parent context stacking order.

sections.text: On real websites, when you click a button and a drop-down menu or pop-up modal appears, we give it a very high z-index like 999 or 1000 to ensure it renders above all page content without anything covering it.
sections.code:
Pop-up menu
Page content
sections.output: A black pop-up menu appears clearly above the gray content thanks to high z-index.

reference.name: z-index
reference.desc: Sets the vertical stacking order of a positioned element (Z-axis).

reference.name: position: absolute
reference.desc: Positions an element at exact coordinates and allows z-index to work.

reference.name: position: relative
reference.desc: Offsets an element from its normal spot and enables z-index layers.

reference.name: position: static
reference.desc: Default element positioning where z-index is ignored.

reference.name: stacking context
reference.desc: The grouping and ordering of layers and elements within a container.

reference.name: auto
reference.desc: Default z-index value which does not create a new stacking context.

exercises.q: Write CSS code to make an absolute positioned element appear on the top layer with a z-index of 50.
Why doesn't z-index work on an element with position: static?
exercises.a: Because the z-index property requires the element to be positioned (non-static) for stacking rules to apply.

exercises.q: How can you make an element hide beneath other elements using z-index?
exercises.a: By giving it a negative value such as z-index: -1.
